title: ירושלים - איזור ממילא (Jerusalem, Mamilla area)
author: R. Reich, E. Shukron, Y. Billig
location_note: c. 100 m south-west of the Old City wall, upper Hinnom valley slope.
notes: CLAIM: the crypt may be the common grave 'Mamilla' of the Christians killed in 614 CE. Unused Byzantine lamps hidden in a bench of the chapel (coded as a concealed group).

features.subtype: rock-cut trench grave (tomb 1) and tomb 5 (benches around a standing pit, repository with use layers to the Hasmonean period)
features.period: tomb 1 Second Temple (Hellenistic flask, Hasmonean coin); tomb 5 First Temple to Hasmonean (coins of Alexander Jannaeus in the top layer)
features.quote: קבר זה הוא מן הבודדים מימי הבית השני בירושלים

features.subtype: tomb 7: benches around a standing pit, repository
features.period: end of the First Temple period (7th-early 6th c. BCE)

features.subtype: chapel with crypt and burial cave (cave 10) full of human bones
features.quote: שהמערה והקריפטה שימשו לאורך זמן ארוך בתקופה

features.subtype: dozens of unused Byzantine oil lamps hidden inside a bench of the chapel

title: ירושלים - שכונת עזרת תורה (Jerusalem, ʿEzrat Torah)
author: Z. Greenhut

features.subtype: rock-cut burial cave: entrance hall, central chamber, three burial units with arcosolia troughs and small inner cells (probably for ossuaries)
features.period: end of the Second Temple period, i.e. late 1st-2nd c. CE (report's wording); no finds
features.quote: שיש לתארך את המערה לשלהי ימי הבית ,השני

features.subtype: underground channel joining the spring cave to the plastered pool at ʿEin Sataf, two building phases
features.period: first phase not dated; later phase Mamluk
features.quote: לתעלה תת־קרקעית שחיברה בין מערת המעיין

features.subtype: spring cave (roof collapse over the channel)
rock-cut cave with square chamber, standing pit and four kokhim
features.quote: המימצא הקיראמי במערה מיוחס לתקופות הרומית הקדומה

features.subtype: plastered cave in the farm courtyard
features.period: pottery around the building Early Roman

features.subtype: large winepress with four plastered semicircular basins, two more winepresses and cupmarks
features.period: pottery around the building Early Roman

title: המערה ׳התלויה׳ של חריטון (The 'Suspended' Cave of Chariton)
author: Y. Hirschfeld
location_note: South cliff of Nahal Teqoa (Wadi Khureitun), c. 800 m south of the monastery of Chariton; no map reference; zone from the gazetteer name (Chariton, Z3).

features.subtype: three natural spaces one above the other (main hall, middle level, Chariton's upper hermit cell), plastered, wall paintings
features.period: Byzantine (sherds under the floor only Byzantine)

features.subtype: three interconnected cisterns in the cave floor, the central one vaulted (c. 25 m3)
features.quote: נתגלו שלושה בורות הקשורים זה לזה

features.subtype: rock-cut channels, pits and clay pipes draining seepage water to the cisterns; channels on the rock shelf
built plastered immersion basin by the cave entrance (2 x 0.8 m), last link of the cistern chain (excavator: immersion basin, Christian)
